item.text: I’ve got the core shape already: 2024 Russian politics is an engineered one-party system with a controlled election, closed media space, and no real opposition contestability. I’m filling a few specific gaps now: official election mechanics, constitutional/term-limit facts, media repression, and whether any 2024 counterevidence or limited remedy exists.

item.text:
**Reused evidence**
- `E0005` [Putin 2024](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2024/03/21/putin-2024) -> `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.10`
- `E0043` [Russian anti-war Putin rival Nadezhdin says he has been barred from election](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/russian-anti-war-putin-rival-091459257.html) -> `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`
- `E0044` [Information on protests in memory of Alexei Navalny 16-19th February](https://ovd.info/en/advocacy/information-protests-memory-alexei-navalny) -> `4B.3`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`
- `E0045` [Repression in Russia in 2024: OVD-Info Overview](https://ovd.info/en/repression-russia-2024-ovd-info-overview?m-message-click-id=9edb42c6-7176-4d56-bc72-32b032dce699&m-message-key-id=-9223372032496631808) -> `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`
- `E0046` [Repressions Report. January 2024](https://ovd.info/en/repressions-report-january-2024) -> `4B.3`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`
- `E0048` [Russia: Officials target drag show in first-ever LGBTI-related 'extremism' case](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/russia-officials-target-drag-show-in-first-ever-lgbti-related-extremism-case) -> `4B.7`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`
- `E0049` [Update on Human Rights in the Russian Federation and the Continuing Need for a Special Rapporteur on Russia](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/28/update-human-rights-russian-federation-and-continuing-need-special-rapporteur) -> `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.6`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`
- `E0009` [Russia: Repressive Laws Used to Crush Civic Freedoms](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/07/russia-repressive-laws-used-crush-civic-freedoms) -> `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

**New evidence**
- [Russian Federation flouts international commitments once again with decision not to invite OSCE observers to presidential election](https://odihr.osce.org/odihr/elections/russia/562065) | OSCE ODIHR | `2024-01-29`
  - Precise claim: Russia did not invite OSCE observers to the 2024 presidential election, denying an impartial independent assessment.
  - Locator: press-release body, opening paragraphs.
  - Source type and credibility: primary election-monitoring institution; very high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 election-process evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: attributable to the Kremlin under Putin; the act is institutional, not a single-person courtroom fact.
  - Contrary points: the Russian delegation later claimed this was an internal sovereign choice, but that does not change the loss of independent observation.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.10`

- [Targeting of dissent in the Russian Federation is alarming and fundamentally undermines human rights and democracy, human rights office ODIHR says](https://odihr.osce.org/odihr/elections/russia/564329) | OSCE ODIHR | `2024-03`
  - Precise claim: ODIHR said targeting dissent undermines democracy and condemned Russia’s decision to hold the election in occupied Ukrainian territories.
  - Locator: press-release summary.
  - Source type and credibility: primary OSCE democracy body; very high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 election-period evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: directly tied to Putin’s political system and election management; not a personal order document.
  - Contrary points: Russia framed the election as lawful and routine, but OSCE said the occupied-territory vote was illegal.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.7`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`

- [Постановление Центральной избирательной комиссии Российской Федерации ... "О результатах выборов Президента Российской Федерации"](https://rg.ru/documents/2024/03/21/cik-post-resultaty2024-site-dok.html) | Российская газета / CEC | `2024-03-21`
  - Precise claim: the official CEC result declared Putin elected with 87.28% and 76,277,708 votes.
  - Locator: opening decision text, пункты 1-2.
  - Source type and credibility: official election authority publication; very high for the stated tally, not for democratic quality.
  - Temporal fit: exact 2024 election result.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: formal institutional confirmation of Putin’s mandate.
  - Contrary points: the official tally does not answer whether the contest was free or fair.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`

- [Vladimir Putin has been sworn in as President of Russia](https://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/73981) | Kremlin.ru | `2024-05-07`
  - Precise claim: Putin was sworn in on May 7, 2024, beginning a new term.
  - Locator: event title and date on the official Kremlin page.
  - Source type and credibility: primary official state source; very high for the ceremonial act.
  - Temporal fit: exact start of the 2024 term.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: directly records Putin’s assumption of office; it does not speak to democratic legitimacy.
  - Contrary points: the ceremonial transfer was constitutionally formal, but occurred after a non-competitive election.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.8`, `4B.10`

- [President of Russia](https://en.kremlin.ru/structure/president) | Kremlin.ru | `current official structure page`
  - Precise claim: the presidency is the head of state, elected for a 6-year term, with constitutional authority and oath obligations.
  - Locator: opening section and authority summary.
  - Source type and credibility: primary constitutional/institutional framing; high for formal powers.
  - Temporal fit: stable baseline for 2024 office and term structure.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: describes the office Putin occupied, not his conduct.
  - Contrary points: the page presents constitutional legitimacy, which contrasts with outside assessments of electoral closure.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.4`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`

- [Russian anti-war Putin rival Nadezhdin says he has been barred from election](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/russian-anti-war-putin-rival-091459257.html) | Reuters | `2024-02-08`
  - Precise claim: the CEC refused to register Boris Nadezhdin, the only serious anti-war challenger, for the March election.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs.
  - Source type and credibility: wire reporting on a direct election event; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct pre-election 2024 evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: institutional exclusion inside Putin’s political order; not proof of a handwritten order, but squarely relevant to entrenchment.
  - Contrary points: Nadezhdin said he would appeal, showing formal process existed, but it did not restore meaningful competition.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`

- [Russian court upholds barring of anti-war presidential candidate Nadezhdin](https://theprint.in/world/russian-court-upholds-barring-of-anti-war-presidential-candidate-nadezhdin/1974536/) | Reuters | `2024-02-22`
  - Precise claim: Russia’s Supreme Court upheld the bar on Nadezhdin, leaving Putin without any significant challenger.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs.
  - Source type and credibility: wire reporting on a legal ruling; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 electoral closure evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: shows the judiciary functioning as part of the entrenchment apparatus.
  - Contrary points: the existence of an appeal path is real, but the outcome confirms the path was not an effective constraint.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.4`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`

- [Putin wants Ukraine ceasefire on current frontlines, sources say](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-wants-ukraine-ceasefire-on-current-frontlines-sources-say-3455927) | Reuters | `2024-05-24`
  - Precise claim: Reuters reported Putin was prepared to freeze the war on current lines if Kyiv and the West did not respond.
  - Locator: lead and second paragraph.
  - Source type and credibility: wire report based on multiple Russian sources; moderately strong but indirect.
  - Temporal fit: relevant mid-2024 peace window.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: suggests tactical willingness to pause fighting, but under terms that preserve Russian gains.
  - Contrary points: the source framing is conditional and self-interested rather than a genuine contestability or pluralism signal.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.10`

- [Putin will cease fire if Ukraine pulls troops from four regions - Reuters](https://theprint.in/world/putin-says-russia-will-cease-fire-if-ukraine-pulls-troops-from-four-regions/2131539/) | Reuters | `2024-06-14`
  - Precise claim: Putin said Russia would cease fire only if Ukraine withdrew from occupied regions and abandoned NATO ambitions.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs and quoted conditions.
  - Source type and credibility: wire report of direct Putin remarks; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: major 2024 conflict/transfer signal.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: direct Putin position, but the terms are maximalist and coercive rather than reciprocal.
  - Contrary points: Putin described it as a route to peace, but the demands functioned as an ultimatum.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.8`, `4B.10`

- [Freedom on the Net 2024: Russia](https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-net/2024) | Freedom House | `2024`
  - Precise claim: Russia’s internet freedom worsened; the government blocked critical sites, developed technical and legal tools against VPNs, and surveilled online critics.
  - Locator: key developments and B1/C5 sections.
  - Source type and credibility: major rights monitor; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: coverage period `June 1, 2023 – May 31, 2024`, so it captures the 2024 environment directly.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: strong evidence of Putin-era censorship architecture, though not every block is personally ordered by him.
  - Contrary points: the report is internet-specific, so it does not by itself prove broader political contestability.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

- [YouTube slowdown in Russia darkens freedom of speech outlook](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/youtube-slowdown-in-russia-darkens-freedom-of-speech-outlook-3562249) | Reuters | `2024-08-08`
  - Precise claim: Russia throttled YouTube, one of the last major foreign platforms for opposition speech, amid a broader censorship drive.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs.
  - Source type and credibility: wire report with technical and civil-society corroboration; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 censorship evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: attributable to Roskomnadzor and the broader Kremlin censorship system under Putin.
  - Contrary points: Russian lawmakers claimed the problem was Google’s failure to upgrade equipment, but Reuters notes experts disputed that explanation.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

- [CPJ: Russia’s YouTube slow down another blow to independent reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/08/cpj-russias-youtube-slow-down-another-blow-to-independent-reporting/) | Committee to Protect Journalists | `2024-08-07`
  - Precise claim: CPJ said the YouTube slowdown was another form of censoring news available to Russian audiences.
  - Locator: alert headline and first paragraph.
  - Source type and credibility: press-freedom NGO; high credibility as corroboration.
  - Temporal fit: direct August 2024 evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: confirms the effect on independent reporting, but not the exact technical trigger.
  - Contrary points: none material beyond the fact that it is advocacy-based reporting.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

- [Russia | RSF](https://rsf.org/en/country/russia) and [Europe - Central Asia: Russia](https://rsf.org/en/classement/2024/europe-central-asia) | RSF | `2024`
  - Precise claim: RSF says almost all independent media were banned or labeled foreign agents, the media are under military censorship, and Russia ranked 162nd in the 2024 press-freedom index.
  - Locator: country-page media landscape and regional index summary.
  - Source type and credibility: major press-freedom monitor; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: 2024 index year.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: strong for the media environment under Putin, less direct on electoral mechanics.
  - Contrary points: ranking movements can reflect changes in other countries too, so the rank should not be overread as a pure year-on-year domestic delta.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.6`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

- [Repression in Russia in 2024: OVD-Info Overview](https://ovd.info/en/repression-russia-2024-ovd-info-overview?m-message-click-id=9edb42c6-7176-4d56-bc72-32b032dce699&m-message-key-id=-9223372032496631808) | OVD-Info | `2025-01-12`
  - Precise claim: the overview records 2024 arrests at rallies, repression around Navalny events, additional foreign-agent designations, and intensified persecution of LGBTQ+ people.
  - Locator: summary metrics and overview section.
  - Source type and credibility: independent Russian rights monitor; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: retrospective but directly about 2024.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: shows the year’s repression pattern inside Putin’s system, though some cases are regional or prosecutorial rather than personally ordered.
  - Contrary points: the August prisoner exchange is a partial remedial counterpoint, but it is exceptional rather than systemic.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.7`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

- [Russia: Officials target drag show in first-ever LGBTI-related 'extremism' case](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/russia-officials-target-drag-show-in-first-ever-lgbti-related-extremism-case/) | Amnesty International | `2024-03-19`
  - Precise claim: Russian authorities opened the first LGBTI-extremism case after the Orenburg drag-show raid.
  - Locator: opening paragraphs.
  - Source type and credibility: major human-rights NGO; high credibility for the existence of the prosecution.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 vulnerable-group repression.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: a national legal regime under Putin enabled the prosecution, though the immediate action was by local law enforcement.
  - Contrary points: one local case does not alone establish nationwide policy, but Amnesty treats it as a national escalation.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.7`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

- [Update on Human Rights in the Russian Federation and the Continuing Need for a Special Rapporteur on Russia](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/28/update-human-rights-russian-federation-and-continuing-need-special-rapporteur) | Human Rights Watch | `2024-08-28`
  - Precise claim: HRW says the Kremlin eliminated genuine political competition, blocked independent candidates, used anti-extremism laws against opposition structures, and kept many anti-war critics imprisoned.
  - Locator: summary and opening discussion.
  - Source type and credibility: major rights NGO synthesis; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 political-freedom assessment.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: strongly attributable to Putin’s regime, though the cited acts involve multiple state organs.
  - Contrary points: the August prisoner swap shows occasional release, but not an independent or durable constraint.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.1`, `4B.2`, `4B.3`, `4B.4`, `4B.5`, `4B.6`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

- [Russia: Repressive Laws Used to Crush Civic Freedoms](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/07/russia-repressive-laws-used-crush-civic-freedoms) | Human Rights Watch | `2024-08-07`
  - Precise claim: HRW says hundreds were jailed or imprisoned under repressive laws and that open discussion has been sharply narrowed.
  - Locator: lines around the opening summary and key examples.
  - Source type and credibility: major rights NGO; high credibility.
  - Temporal fit: direct 2024 evidence.
  - Ruler attribution and limits: reflects the Putin-era legal regime, though not all enforcement decisions are personally signed by him.
  - Contrary points: the report is broad and thematic, so it works best as systemic corroboration rather than an event-by-event record.
  - Exact lenses: `4B.3`, `4B.6`, `4B.8`, `4B.9`, `4B.10`

**Search and rejection summary**
- I considered roughly 30 documents across OSCE/ODIHR, Kremlin pages, CEC/TASS/RG, Reuters wires and syndications, Freedom House, RSF, CPJ, OVD-Info, HRW, Amnesty, Meduza, and a few secondary republications.
- I kept sources that directly affected the 2024 contestability, media space, term/transfer, or digital-control questions.
- I rejected duplicate Reuters republications and image-only pages when they repeated the same facts without adding new evidence.
- I rejected older background items when they only restated Putin’s long-run authoritarianism without adding 2024-specific signal.
- I rejected more general rights reports when they were redundant with the stronger election-specific and media-censorship sources already retained.
- Several Kremlin transcript pages timed out, so I relied on accessible official index pages and Reuters/OSCE republished coverage of the same dated events.

**Remaining gaps**
- Direct evidence of internal elite bargaining and whether any real institutional constraint operated on Putin in 2024 is still thin.
- The exact mechanics of turnout inflation, pressure on voters, and administrative coercion are only partly visible in open sources.
- Attribution is strong at the system level, but more granular evidence would help separate Putin’s own direction from Roskomnadzor, the CEC, courts, and regional officials.
- OSCE could not observe the election, which is itself highly probative, but it also means the outside record is less granular than in more open systems.
